In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Qatadah said: they were an unlettered people, and no warner had come to them before Muhammad (peace be upon him). Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said: this refers to the interval (al-fatrah, the period without prophets) that was between 'Isa and Muhammad (peace be upon them both). "So that they may be guided."

"Allah is He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne. You have, besides Him, neither protector nor intercessor. Will you not then remember?" The measure of his journey is a thousand years: five hundred for his descent from the heaven to the earth, and five hundred for his ascent from the earth to the heaven. The distance between the heaven and the earth is a five-hundred-year journey; he means that if any of the children of Adam were to travel it, he would not complete it except in a thousand years, while the angels cover this distance in one day. Ibn 'Abbas said to him: "Who are you?" He said: "I am Abdullah ibn Fayruz, freedman of Uthman ibn Affan." Abdullah ibn 'Abbas said: "Days that Allah named; I do not know what they are, and I dislike to say in the Book of Allah what I do not know." His saying: "That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Mighty, the Merciful. He who perfected everything He created." Nafi' and the people of Kufa read (khalaqahu) with a fathah on the lam, as a verb, and Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose this reading, and then said: "because it is easier in meaning." It is the reading of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. The others read it with a sukun on the lam. Al-Akhfash said: it is in apposition (badal), and its meaning is: "He who perfected the creation of everything."

Ibn 'Abbas said: He perfected it and made it firm. Then he said: "Indeed, the anus of the monkey is not beautiful, but He made its creation firm." Qatadah said: "He made it beautiful." Muqatil said: "He knew how to create everything," from your saying "so-and-so is good at (yuhsinu) such-and-such," meaning he knows it.

"And He began the creation of man," meaning Adam (peace be upon him), "from clay. Then He made his offspring, his descendants, from a lineage (sulalah), from a fluid (nutfah)." It was so named because it issues (tansulu) from the human being, that is, it comes out; and from this the child is called sulalah.

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the best (safw) of water, "from a despised (muhin) water," weak. "Then He proportioned him and breathed into him of His spirit, and made for you hearing, sight and hearts; little are you grateful." "And they said," meaning the deniers of resurrection: "When we are lost (dallalna) in the earth?" that is, when we are destroyed, become nullified, and become dust. Its root is from the Arabs' saying: "dalla al-ma' fi al-laban" when it perishes; and it is said: "adlaltu al-mayyit," meaning I buried the dead. The poet said:

Ibn Muhaysin read (dalalna) with a kasrah on the lam, and this is a dialect.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: "Say: The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will take you (yatawaffakum) by taking your souls," Mujahid said: "The earth was gathered for him, and it became for him like a tray, from which he takes wherever he wills." Muqatil and al-Kalbi said:

We have been told that the name of the angel of death is 'Azra'il, and he has four wings: one wing in the east, one wing in the west, one wing at the furthest edge of the world from where the east wind comes, and one wing from the other horizon. He has one foot in the east and the other in the west, and creation is between his feet; his head and body are as far apart as between the heaven and the earth. The world has been made for him like the palm of a hand; its owner takes from it whatever he loves without hardship or toil; that is, it is like a brick before him. He takes the souls of creatures in the eastern and western parts of the earth, and he has helpers from the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, from Abdullah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik, from al-Khattab ibn Ahmad ibn 'Isa, who said: Abu Nafi' Ahmad ibn Kathir informed me, from Kathir ibn Hisham, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Indeed, the stride of the angel of death is the distance between the east and the west."

The angel of death entered upon Sulayman, and he kept looking at a man among his companions, looking at him continuously. When he left, the man said: "Who is this?" He said: "This is the angel of death." The man said: "He was looking at me as if he wanted me." Sulayman said: "What do you want?" He said: "I want you to carry me on the wind and cast me into India." So he called the wind, and it carried him and cast him into India. Then the angel of death came to Sulayman (peace be upon him) and said: "You were continuously looking at a man among my companions." He said: "I was surprised by him, for I had been commanded to take his soul in India, while he was with you."

The taking (tawaffi) by Allah, glorified is He, is the creation of death. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun, from Hazim ibn Yahya al-Halwani, from Muhammad ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Amr ibn Abi Salamah, from Sadaqah ibn Abdullah, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "An angel came to me with a message from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then he raised one of his feet and placed it above the heaven, and the other on the earth, and did not raise it." [188] [Kanz al-'Ummal 6/136, no. 15153.]

Some of them said its meaning is: "He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth" for the duration of the days of this world; "then the affair and the arrangement ascend to Him," and return to Him after the end of the world and its annihilation, "in a day whose measure is a thousand years of what you count," and this is the Day of Resurrection.

As for His saying "fifty thousand years" [Al-Ma'arij 70:4], He meant for the disbelievers: Allah makes that day, for them, the measure of fifty thousand years, while for the believer it is like the time of an obligatory prayer that he prayed in the house of the world. It is also permissible that the Day of Resurrection has a beginning and no end, and that it has various times, some of which are a thousand years and some fifty thousand years. It is also permissible that this is a report of its severity, its terror and its hardship, because the Arabs describe days of hardship as long and days of joy as short; and a group of exegetes adopted this interpretation.

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me, saying: Abdullah ibn Fayruz, a freedman of Uthman ibn Affan, and I entered upon Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Fayruz asked him about this verse. Ibn 'Abbas said to him: "Who are you?" He said: "I am Abdullah ibn Fayruz, freedman of Uthman ibn Affan." Abdullah ibn 'Abbas said: "Days that Allah named; I do not know what they are, and I dislike to say in the Book of Allah what I do not know." Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: Time passed until I entered upon Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and he was asked about it and did not know what to say. So I said to him: "Shall I not inform you of what I heard from Ibn 'Abbas?" I informed him, and Ibn al-Musayyab said to the questioner: "This is Ibn 'Abbas, who has refrained from saying anything about it, and he is more knowledgeable than I am."

His saying: "That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Mighty, the Merciful. He who perfected everything He created." Nafi' and the people of Kufa read (khalaqahu) with a fathah on the lam, as a verb, and Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose this reading, and then said: "because it is easier in meaning." It is the reading of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. The others read it with a sukun on the lam. Al-Akhfash said: it is in apposition (badal), and its meaning is: "He who perfected the creation of everything."

Ibn 'Abbas said: He perfected it and made it firm. Then he said: "Indeed, the anus of the monkey is not beautiful, but He made its creation firm." Qatadah said: "He made it beautiful." Muqatil said: "He knew how to create everything," from your saying "so-and-so is good at (yuhsinu) such-and-such," meaning he knows it.

"And He began the creation of man," meaning Adam (peace be upon him), "from clay. Then He made his offspring, his descendants, from a lineage (sulalah), from a fluid (nutfah)." It was so named because it issues (tansulu) from the human being, that is, it comes out; and from this the child is called sulalah.

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the best (safw) of water, "from a despised (muhin) water," weak. "Then He proportioned him and breathed into him of His spirit, and made for you hearing, sight and hearts; little are you grateful." "And they said," meaning the deniers of resurrection: "When we are lost (dallalna) in the earth?" that is, when we are destroyed, become nullified, and become dust. Its root is from the Arabs' saying: "dalla al-ma' fi al-laban" when it perishes; and it is said: "adlaltu al-mayyit," meaning I buried the dead. The poet said:

*And a father they buried without a proper grave, and Jurm and Na'il were left at al-Jawlan.* [Taj al-'Arus 10/76.]

Ibn Muhaysin read (dalalna) with a kasrah on the lam, and this is a dialect.

Al-Hasan and al-A'mash read (salalna) with an unpointed sad [i.e., sad, not dad], meaning "we became putrid," and this is the reading of 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him). [See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Nahhas 1/20; Tafsir al-Qurtubi 14/92; Lisan al-'Arab 11/384.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, from Ibn Shanbah, who said: Abu Hamid al-Mustamli informed me, from Muhammad ibn Hatim [al-Karkhi] [In the Isfahan copy: al-Zamli.] Abu [Uthman] [In the Isfahan copy: 'Imarah.] the grammarian, from al-Musayyab ibn Sharik, from 'Ubaydah al-Dabbi, from a man, from 'Ali, that he read: "a-idha sallalna," meaning "we became putrid."

Muhammad ibn Hatim said: it is said "salla al-lahm" and "asalla" when meat becomes putrid.

"Are we truly in a new creation?" Allah says: "Rather, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord."

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: "Say: The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will take you (yatawaffakum) by taking your souls," Mujahid said: "The earth was gathered for him, and it became for him like a tray, from which he takes wherever he wills." Muqatil and al-Kalbi said:

We have been told that the name of the angel of death is 'Azra'il, and he has four wings: one wing in the east, one wing in the west, one wing at the furthest edge of the world from where the east wind comes, and one wing from the other horizon. He has one foot in the east and the other in the west, and creation is between his feet; his head and body are as far apart as between the heaven and the earth. The world has been made for him like the palm of a hand; its owner takes from it whatever he loves without hardship or toil; that is, it is like a brick before him. He takes the souls of creatures in the eastern and western parts of the earth, and he has helpers from the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, from Abdullah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik, from al-Khattab ibn Ahmad ibn 'Isa, who said: Abu Nafi' Ahmad ibn Kathir informed me, from Kathir ibn Hisham, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Indeed, the stride of the angel of death is the distance between the east and the west."

And al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us, from Abdullah ibn Yusuf, from Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad, from Salamah ibn Shabib, from al-Walid ibn Salamah al-Dimashqi, from Thawr ibn Yazid, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan [In the Isfahan copy: Ma'dan.], from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: "The angel of death has a spear that reaches the distance between the east and the west, and he scrutinizes the faces of people; there is no household except that the angel of death examines them twice each day. When he sees a person whose term has ended, he strikes his head with that spear and says: 'Now you shall be visited by the army of the dead.'"

And al-Husayn ibn Muhammad said: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i informed me, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Numayr, from al-A'mash, from Khaythamah and from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said:

The angel of death entered upon Sulayman, and he kept looking at a man among his companions, looking at him continuously. When he left, the man said: "Who is this?" He said: "This is the angel of death." The man said: "He was looking at me as if he wanted me." Sulayman said: "What do you want?" He said: "I want you to carry me on the wind and cast me into India." So he called the wind, and it carried him and cast him into India. Then the angel of death came to Sulayman (peace be upon him) and said: "You were continuously looking at a man among my companions." He said: "I was surprised by him, for I had been commanded to take his soul in India, while he was with you."

If it is asked: what is the connection between His saying "Our messengers take him (tawaffathu rusuluna)" [Al-An'am 6:61], "the angels take them (tatawaffahum al-malaikah)" [An-Nahl 16:28], "Say: the angel of death takes you (yatawaffakum malak al-mawt)" [As-Sajdah 32:11], His saying "Allah takes the souls at the time of their death (Allah yatawaffa al-anfus hina mawtiha)" [Az-Zumar 39:42], and "It is He who takes you by night (yatawaffakum bi-al-layl)" [Al-An'am 6:60]?

It is answered: the taking (tawaffi) by the angels is the seizing and the drawing out; the taking (tawaffi) by the angel of death is the calling and the command: he calls the spirits and they respond, then he commands his helpers to seize them. The taking (tawaffi) by Allah, glorified is He, is the creation of death. And Allah knows best.

The Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 32, verses 12–22:

Allah's words: ﴿If only you could see when the guilty ones will hang their heads before their Lord, in shame before Him for what they committed of sins in the world, saying: "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so send us back, and we will do righteous deeds; indeed we are now certain."﴾ "Hanging their heads" (nakisu ru'usihim) means lowering their heads (mu'tati'u ru'usihim). The answer to "law" (if only) is omitted, and its implied meaning is: "you would have seen a wondrous thing."

﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾, meaning its right direction and its success in faith. ﴿But the word from Me has come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together."﴾ This is His saying to Iblis: ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with you and those among them who follow you, all together."﴾

Then it is said to the people of the Fire: ﴿"So taste [the punishment] because you forgot the meeting of this your Day"﴾, meaning you abandoned faith in it. ﴿Indeed We have forgotten you﴾, meaning We have left you in the Fire. ﴿And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do.﴾

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Majah al-Qazwini, from al-Hasan ibn Ayyub al-Qazwini, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatawani, from Sayyar, from Hammad al-Saffar, from Hajjaj al-Aswad, from Jabalah, from a client of his, from Ka'b who said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the angels will stand and intercede, then the prophets will stand and intercede, then the martyrs will stand and intercede, then the believers will stand and intercede, until all intercession has come to an end and no one is left. Then Mercy will come forth and say: 'O Lord, I am Mercy, so grant me intercession.' He will say: 'I have granted it to you.' She will say: 'O Lord, for whom?' He will say: 'For whoever remembered Me in a station and feared Me in it, or hoped in Me, or called upon Me with one supplication; whoever feared Me or hoped in Me, bring them out.'" He said: "So they will come out, and there will remain in the Fire no one whom Allah regards with any consideration. Then its people will be greatly distressed by it. Then He will command the Fire, and it will seize them, and no soul will ever enter it again, and no grief will ever leave it."

It is also said: ﴿"Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day."﴾

Allah's words: ﴿Only those believe in Our signs who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and glorify the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant﴾, meaning they are not arrogant toward faith in Him or toward prostrating to Him. ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾: "tatajafa" means they rise and withdraw; it is a form of "tafa'ul" from "al-jafa'" (distance, separation). The Arabs say: "jaffa zahraka 'an al-jidar" (he kept his back away from the wall), and "jafat 'ayn fulan 'an al-ghamd" (the eye of so-and-so did not close in sleep) when he did not sleep.

Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed me, saying: Abu Amr Uthman ibn Ahmad ibn Sam'an al-Wazzan informed me, from Abdullah ibn Qahtaba ibn Marzuq, from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harshi, from al-Harith ibn Wahiya al-Rasibi who said: I heard Malik ibn Dinar say: I asked Anas ibn Malik about the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾. Anas said: "Some of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray from the Maghrib prayer until the late 'Isha' prayer, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds.﴾"

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad [from Musa ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn Muhammad] informed me, from al-Hasan ibn Alawayh, from Isma'il ibn Isa, from al-Musayyab, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik who said: "It was revealed about us, the group of the Ansar: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, the verse. We used to pray the Maghrib, and we would not return to our homes until we prayed the 'Isha' with the Prophet (ﷺ)."

We were also informed by al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim ibn Ali ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Wahb, from Muhammad ibn Humayd, from Yahya ibn al-Durays, from al-Nadr ibn Humayd, from Sa'id, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever prays after the Maghrib until the 'Isha' will have built for him in Paradise two palaces [between which is] a distance of [a hundred] years' travel, and in them are trees such that if the people of the East and the people of the West were to dwell in them, they would be sufficed with fruit. This is the prayer of the penitent (al-awwabin) and the heedlessness of the heedless. Indeed, among the accepted supplications that are not rejected is the supplication between the Maghrib and the 'Isha'."[189] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 7/392, no. 19450.]]

Ata' said: It means they pray the 'atamah (the night prayer, 'Isha') and do not sleep through it. This is supported by what Abdullah ibn Hamid informed me, from Abd al-Samad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mukarram, from al-Sari ibn Sahl, from Abdullah ibn Rashid who said: Abu Ubaydah Mujja'a ibn al-Zubayr informed me, from Aban who said: A woman came to Anas ibn Malik and said: "I sleep before the 'Isha'." He said: "Do not sleep, for this verse was revealed about those who do not sleep before the late 'Isha': ﴿Their sides forsake their beds.﴾"

Abu al-Aliyah, al-Hasan, Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: it refers to tahajjud and the night prayer (qiyam al-layl). The evidence for this interpretation is what

Abu Abdullah ibn Fanjawayh informed us, from Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from his father, from Zayd ibn al-Hubab, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Asim, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Mu'adh, from the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope﴾, he said: "The servant's standing in prayer at night."

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Asfahani informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Hamadhani, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dabari, from Abd al-Razzaq ibn Mu'ammar, from Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Wa'il, from Mu'adh who said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey. I was close to him as we were traveling, and I said: 'O Prophet of Allah, will you not tell me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise and keep me far from the Fire?' He said: 'O Mu'adh, you have asked about something great, and it is easy for the one whom Allah makes it easy for: you worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, you establish the prayer, you pay the zakat, you fast Ramadan, and you perform the Hajj to the House.' Then he said: 'Shall I not direct you to the gates of good? Fasting is a shield from the Fire, charity extinguishes sin (in the source: "the wrath of the Lord" is replaced by "sin"), and a man's prayer in the depth of the night.' Then he recited: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds … as a reward for what they used to do﴾ until he reached ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾. Then he said: 'Shall I not tell you of the head of the matter, its pillar and the peak of its hump?' [In the source there is an addition: 'the head of the matter, its pillar and the peak of its hump' – I said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The head of the matter is the prayer, its pillar is the prayer, and the peak of its hump is jihad.' Then he said: 'Shall I not tell you the key to all of that?'] I said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He took hold of his tongue and said: 'Restrain this.'

I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, will we be held accountable for what we say?' He said: 'May your mother lose you, O Mu'adh! Do people get thrown on their faces or on their noses into the Fire except for the harvest of their tongues?'"[190] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/231; Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1314, no. 3973.]]

Al-Dahhak said: it is that a man prays the 'Isha' and the morning prayer in congregation.

Al-Husayn ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Majah who said: Abu Awana al-Kufi informed me at al-Rayy, from Minjab ibn al-Harith, from Ali ibn Mushir, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah gathers the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, a caller will come and call with a voice that all creatures will hear: 'Today the people of the gathering will know who is most worthy of honour.' Then he will return and call: 'Let those whose sides forsook their beds stand up.' They will stand, and they will be few. Then he will return and call: 'Let those who praised Allah in adversity and hardship stand up.' They will stand, and they will be few. They will all proceed together to Paradise, and then the rest of the people will be judged."[191] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/102.]]

﴿Calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend from what We have provided them.﴾ ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾, meaning what is concealed for them. This is the reading of the majority (al-'amma). Hamza and Ya'qub read "ukhfi" (with the first person, "I conceal") with the yā' (as an independent form), and their argument is the reading of Abdullah: "nukhfi" with the nun. Muhammad ibn Ka'b read "akhfa" with an alif, meaning: "Allah has concealed from them the comfort for the eyes." The reading of the majority is in the singular (tawhid).

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, from Makki ibn Abdan, from Abdullah ibn Hashim who said: Abu Mu'awiya informed me, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted says: 'I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.'" Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And what I have shown you of its lowest (bullahu) is more…" Recite if you wish: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes.﴾[192] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1447, no. 4328; in the Qur'an the word is "qurrah" (singular).]] ﴿As a reward for what they used to do.﴾ He said: Abu Hurayrah used to recite it thus: "qurrat a'yun" (plural).

Ibn Mas'ud said: "It is written in the Torah: 'Allah has prepared for those whose sides forsake their beds what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, and what no near angel knows.' And indeed it is in the Qur'an: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾, the verse."

His words: ﴿Is one who is a believer like one who is a defiant sinner? They are not equal﴾, the verse.

It was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib and al-Walid ibn Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt, the half-brother of Uthman through their mother. The reason was that there was a dispute and an exchange of words between them about something. Al-Walid said to Ali: "Be quiet, for you are a boy. By Allah, I am more eloquent of tongue than you, sharper of spear, more courageous of heart, and fuller in filling the ranks of the battalion." Ali said to him: "Be quiet, for you are a defiant sinner." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿Is one who is a believer like one who is a defiant sinner? They are not equal.﴾

He said "they are not equal" (la yastawun) rather than "the two are not equal" (la yastawiyan), because by "the believer" he did not intend one believer, nor by "the sinner" one sinner; rather he meant all the sinners and all the believers. Al-Farra' said: when two are not specified as a pair, they are treated in the manner of a plural.

Then He mentioned the condition of the two groups and their end, saying, the Mighty, the Majestic: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will have the Gardens of Refuge as a lodging, as a reward for what they used to do. And as for those who defied, their refuge will be the Fire; whenever they wish to leave it, they will be returned into it, and it will be said to them: "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."﴾ ﴿And We will surely make them taste a punishment nearer than the greater punishment, so that they may return.﴾ Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu al-Aliyah, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan and Ibrahim said: the "nearer punishment" is the calamities of this world, its sicknesses and afflictions, with which Allah tests His servants until they repent. This is the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas.

From Ikrimah, from him: the prescribed punishments (hudud).

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, al-Hasan ibn Ali and Abdullah ibn al-Harith: killing by the sword on the day of Badr.

Muqatil: hunger for seven years in Mecca, until they ate carrion, bones and dogs. Mujahid: the punishment of the grave. They said: "And the greater punishment" is on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿So that they may return﴾ from their disbelief.

Allah's words: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord and then turns away from them? Indeed We will take vengeance upon the guilty (al-mujrimin)﴾, meaning the polytheists. Zayd ibn Rafi' said: by "the guilty" here is meant the people of qadar (divine decree). Then he recited: ﴿Indeed the guilty are in error and madness, … Indeed We have created everything in measure﴾, to His words, [Qur'an 54:47–49].

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni who said: Jamahir ibn Muhammad al-Dimashqi informed me, from Hisham ibn Ammar, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah, from Ubadah ibn Sunni, from Junadah ibn Abi Umayyah, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever does three things has committed a crime: whoever ties a banner for an unjust cause, or disobeys his parents, or walks with a wrongdoer to support him [the last phrase is not in the source] has committed a crime. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed We will take vengeance upon the guilty.﴾"[193] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/90.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Fanjawayh informed me, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Majah who said: Abu Awana al-Kufi informed me at al-Rayy, from Minjab ibn al-Harith, from Ali ibn Mushir, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah gathers the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, a caller will come and call with a voice that all creatures will hear: 'Today the people of the gathering will know who is most worthy of honour.' Then he will return and call: 'Let those who praised Allah in adversity and hardship stand up.' They will stand, and they will be few. ﴿Calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend from what We have provided them.﴾ ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes﴾, meaning what is concealed for them. Hamza and Ya'qub read "ukhfi" (with the first person, "I conceal") with the yā' (as an independent form), and their argument is the reading of Abdullah: "nukhfi" with the nun. Muhammad ibn Ka'b read "akhfa" with an alif, meaning: "Allah has concealed from them the comfort for the eyes." The reading of the majority is in the singular (tawhid).

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, from Makki ibn Abdan, from Abdullah ibn Hashim who said: Abu Mu'awiya informed me, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted says: 'I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.'" Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And what I have shown you of its lowest (bullahu) is more…" Recite if you wish: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes.﴾[192] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1447, no. 4328; in the Qur'an the word is "qurrah" (singular).]] ﴿As a reward for what they used to do.﴾ He said: Abu Hurayrah used to recite it thus: "qurrat a'yun" (plural).

His words: ﴿Is one who is a believer like one who is a defiant sinner? They are not equal﴾, the verse.

The reason was that there was a dispute and an exchange of words between them about something. Al-Walid said to Ali: "Be quiet, for you are a boy. From Ikrimah, from him: the prescribed punishments (hudud).

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, al-Hasan ibn Ali and Abdullah ibn al-Harith: killing by the sword on the day of Badr.

Muqatil: hunger for seven years in Mecca, until they ate carrion, bones and dogs. Mujahid: the punishment of the grave. They said: "And the greater punishment" is on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿So that they may return﴾ from their disbelief.

Allah's words: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord and then turns away from them? Indeed We will take vengeance upon the guilty (al-mujrimin)﴾, meaning the polytheists. Zayd ibn Rafi' said: by "the guilty" here is meant the people of qadar (divine decree). Then he recited: ﴿Indeed the guilty are in error and madness, … Indeed We have created everything in measure﴾, to His words, [Qur'an 54:47–49].

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni who said: Jamahir ibn Muhammad al-Dimashqi informed me, from Hisham ibn Ammar, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah, from Ubadah ibn Sunni, from Junadah ibn Abi Umayyah, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever does three things has committed a crime: whoever ties a banner for an unjust cause, or disobeys his parents, or walks with a wrongdoer to support him [the last phrase is not in the source] has committed a crime. Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 32, verses 23–30:

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, so be not in doubt about meeting him﴾ (on the night of the Mi'raj). It is related from Ibn 'Abbas; and al-Suddi said: [it means] from his receiving the Book of Allah, Exalted is He, with contentment and acceptance. The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: By "meeting" they did not intend seeing, but rather his being in direct contact with the matter, conveying the Message of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and accepting the Book of Allah. It has also been said: "from the meeting with Allah" is addressed to the Prophet (ﷺ), and what is meant is someone other than him.

﴿And We made it [i.e., the Book; Qatadah said: Moses] a guidance for the Children of Israel. And We appointed from among them leaders (a'immah) guiding in goodness, who are followed, who guide [others] by Our command, when they were patient﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read (limā) with a kasra on the lam and a light (unshaddated) mim, meaning "because of their patience," and Abu 'Ubayd preferred this, considering the reading of 'Abdullah, "limā ṣabarū." The rest read it with a fatha on the lam and a shadda on the mim, meaning "when they were patient."

﴿And they were certain of Our signs.﴾ ﴿Indeed your Lord will decide between them﴾, i.e., will judge between them, and the people of Yemen call the judge al-Fayṣal, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ.﴾ ﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, among whose dwellings they walk? Indeed in that are signs. Will they not then hear?﴾ — the signs and admonitions of Allah, so that they may take heed from them.

His saying: ﴿Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land﴾ — i.e., the dry land, the rough one in which there is no vegetation. Its root is from their saying: "a she-camel jarrāz," when she eats everything she finds, and "a man jarūz," when he is a great eater. The rajaz poet said:

*A jarūz beast; when hungry, it weeps, and eats dates without spitting out the pits.*

And "a sword jarrāz" means a cutting one; and "jarrarat al-jarād al-zar'" means the locusts uprooted the crop. So the jurz is the land on whose surface nothing is left but that it spoils it. It has four dialectal forms: jarz, jurz, jarz and jurz. [[See the tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 14/111, at the verse.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is a land in Yemen. Mujahid said: it is Abyan. ﴿Then We bring forth thereby crops, of which their livestock eat, and themselves. Will they not see?﴾

﴿And they say: "When is this victory, if you are truthful?"﴾ Some of them said: By the Day of Victory he meant the Day of Resurrection, in which there is reward and punishment and judgment among the servants.

Qatadah said: The companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed we have a day in which we will be blessed and find rest, and He will judge between us and you." So the disbelievers said mockingly: ﴿When is this victory?﴾ — i.e., the decision and judgment.

Al-Kalbi said: it means the conquest of Makkah. Al-Suddi said: it means the Day of Badr, because the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say to them: "Indeed Allah is our helper and will make us victorious over you."

﴿Say: "On the Day of Victory" — the Day of Resurrection — "the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved."﴾ Whoever interprets "victory" as help says: their faith will not benefit them when the punishment comes and they are killed.

﴿So turn away from them and wait; indeed they are waiting.﴾ The common reading is muntaẓirūn with a kasra on the ẓā'. Muhammad ibn al-Sumaify’ read it with a fatha on the ẓā'. Al-Farra' said: this is not valid except by supposing an implied meaning: "indeed they are waiting for their Lord." Abu Hatim said: the correct reading is with a kasra, because of His saying: ﴿So wait; indeed they are waiting﴾ [[Surat al-Dukhan: 59.]].
